zh.title: 松山機場如何迎接新世代廣體客機？長榮787-10進駐與華航A350的差異
zh.summary: 長榮787-10歷經2020年試停、停機線與空橋等設施評估，2023年正式執飛松山－羽田及虹橋航線。華航A350-900翼展較787-10更寬，其松山機坪與滑行道適用性仍有不同考量。
body: 臺北松山機場（TSA）位處市中心，腹地與地面作業空間有限。近年新世代廣體客機逐漸投入臺灣航線，其中長榮航空已將波音787-10安排於松山往返東京羽田及上海虹橋（SHA），華航的Airbus A350-900則主要從桃園機場執飛。兩種代表性廣體機型為何有不同的機場配置，必須從停機位、翼展與地面作業條件觀察。

長榮787-10能夠進駐松山，經歷了具體的評估與準備。2020年4月16日，長榮以787-10飛抵松山測試停機位，檢查停止線、空橋接靠、翼尖及機尾淨空等項目；當時有停機位因空橋條件未能順利接靠。松山機場安全管理教材亦記載，因應787-10曾規劃調整停止線及淨空標線、配合實機試停確認空橋和勤務道路間距，並將787-10納入E類航機滑行道改善及5至7號停機位橋電設備更新規劃。這些是航空站配合新機型進駐的設施調整與風險降低措施，不能理解為整座機坪全面改建。
經過場站準備，長榮在2023年8月22日正式安排787-10執飛松山－羽田BR190，並宣布投入松山－羽田及松山－虹橋航線。長榮公布787-10配置342席，比原有A330-300增加約10%座位，可在都市機場既有時段限制下提高單班運能。
民航局目前生效的《臺北飛航情報區飛航指南》（2026年10月1日版本）顯示，臺北松山機場10／28跑道長2,605公尺、寬60公尺。其停機位資料將3、9號位的最大機型列為A330-300，4至7號位則列為波音777-200，並未列出A350-900。這些是公開的標準機坪配置資料，不能單憑此斷言A350在任何情況下都不得降落松山，但足以說明若要安排常態營運，必須先處理停機位及地面動線的適用性問題。
翼展是兩款航機的重要差異。波音787-10翼展約60.1公尺，空中巴士A350-900則達64.75公尺，約寬4.6公尺。即使兩者皆屬ICAO機場參考代碼E類航機，同類別並不表示停機位、空橋與滑行路徑可以不經評估直接共用。松山針對787-10完成的設施調整與試停結果，也不能自動套用至A350。
另一方面，2,605公尺跑道並不等於所有A350都「絕對無法起降」。實際可用起降性能須依機型、起降重量、氣溫、風、跑道狀況、障礙物與特定程序計算，航空公司還須完成相關運作評估。松山機場位於市區，民航局亦將其列為受到地形及建築物障礙影響的特殊機場，航機必須符合離場爬升梯度等規定。現有公開資料不足以確認華航A350在何種載重及條件下可於松山安全起降，更不能將跑道長度當作唯一判斷標準。
日本羽田機場（HND）已有日本航空A350-1000營運，並非機型進不去羽田的問題。長榮以787-10投入松山－羽田及虹橋，華航則在松山－羽田維持A330系列，而A350主要服務桃園出發的航線；航班安排仍涉及機隊分配、載客需求及機場運作條件，不能僅由一項機場規格推定航空公司的全部決策。
現階段公開資料並未證實華航A350-900在松山機場遭到全面禁止，也沒有公布華航正式引進A350執飛松山航線的計畫。從長榮787-10進駐過程可見，機場能否使用某款新機型，需逐項完成停機位、地面動線與飛航性能評估，不能只靠跑道長度或機型所屬類別判定。

en.title: Songshan Airport's Widebody Challenge: EVA Air's 787-10 and China Airlines' A350
en.summary: EVA Air trialled the Boeing 787-10 at Songshan in 2020 before launching scheduled flights in 2023. The wider Airbus A350-900 poses different stand and taxiway compatibility considerations.
body: Taipei Songshan Airport (TSA) is a city-center airport with constrained ground operating space. EVA Air now operates Boeing 787-10 flights from Songshan to Tokyo Haneda and Shanghai Hongqiao, while China Airlines predominantly deploys its Airbus A350-900 from Taoyuan. Understanding the different aircraft assignments involves stand compatibility, wingspan and operational requirements.

EVA Air's 787-10 was trial-parked at Songshan on April 16, 2020. The trials examined aircraft stop lines, passenger boarding bridges, wingtip clearances and tail-to-service-road distances; one parking position initially faced a bridge compatibility issue. Songshan Airport safety-management materials document mitigation plans including revised markings, on-aircraft stand trials, Code E taxiway preparations and planned electrical-equipment changes at stands 5–7. These targeted adjustments should not be confused with a wholesale rebuilding of the apron.

On August 22, 2023, EVA Air launched scheduled 787-10 operations at Songshan with flight BR190 to Haneda and announced deployment to both Haneda and Hongqiao. The airline stated that the 342-seat aircraft offered approximately ten percent more capacity than its A330-300.

Taiwan's currently effective aeronautical information publication, dated October 1, 2026, lists Songshan's Runway 10/28 as 2,605 meters long and 60 meters wide. Aircraft stand data specify the A330-300 as the maximum type for stands 3 and 9 and the Boeing 777-200 for stands 4 through 7; the A350-900 is not listed. This does not by itself establish an absolute prohibition on A350 landings, but it raises a practical question about the aircraft's suitability for routine ground operations.

Wingspan is a key distinction: approximately 60.1 meters for the Boeing 787-10 and 64.75 meters for the Airbus A350-900. Although both are ICAO Code E aircraft, that designation does not guarantee identical clearance, taxiway, stand or boarding-bridge compatibility. The adaptations made for the 787-10 do not automatically authorize the A350.

A 2,605-meter runway alone does not prove that every A350 operation would be impossible. Performance depends on aircraft mass, temperature, wind, runway conditions, obstacles and relevant procedures. Songshan is designated a special airport due to terrain and building obstructions, with mandatory departure climb gradients. The public information reviewed here does not establish exactly which A350 loading conditions, if any, could support a specific Songshan operation.

Tokyo Haneda already accommodates A350 aircraft, including Japan Airlines' A350-1000. EVA Air's Songshan–Haneda and Songshan–Hongqiao operations use the 787-10, while China Airlines continues to use the A330 family from Songshan and concentrates A350 flying at Taoyuan. Deployment decisions also depend on demand, fleet availability and airport operating conditions.

Public information does not establish a blanket ban on A350-900 operations at Songshan, nor an announced China Airlines plan to introduce the type there. EVA Air's 787-10 introduction illustrates why each new widebody aircraft requires specific stand, taxiway and flight-performance assessments rather than a runway-length comparison alone.
